subject: Post-call recap & benchmarks — model fit recommendations
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>
To: Alice Nguyen <alice@acme.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps (model fit)

Hi Alice / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today — really helpful to understand Acme's low-latency inference constraints for the customer support agent (median response time target ~300ms, occasional bursts during business hours). Quick recap + recommended next steps: 

1) Model fit: Based on the prompt examples and safety/QA requirements you shared, we think the best balance of throughput and quality for initial evals is:
   - redwood-13b-q8 (recommended): strong quality for instruction following + reasonable cost
   - redwood-7b-q4 (fast, lower cost): good for high-throughput shallow tasks
   - redwood-rlhf-small-v1 (safety-tuned): use for sensitive flows or fallback

2) Benchmarks & prompts: I attached a short benchmark summary and the prompt set we used in the call. I'll also share a Drive folder with full Redwood-verified performance profiles (TPS and latency percentiles) for those models.

3) Next steps:
   - I'll drop the benchmark links and a short runbook for running a 24-hour eval (sample config + target workloads).
   - Marissa (copied) will help with a quick test harness and do one run on Dedicated if you want isolated capacity.
   - If acceptable, propose a week-long sandbox (1 GPU, sample data) to validate latency tail behavior and quality regressions.

Can you confirm which date next week works for a quick sync to lock the evaluation scope?

Thanks,
Alex

Thanks Alex — that recap is spot on. A couple quick clarifying Qs before we schedule: 

- For the redwood-13b-q8 recommendation, what are the expected 95th/99th latency percentiles at our target concurrency (we expect ~15 tps during peak)?
- Any quality regression risk we should be watching for when moving from the 13b to the 7b model? We have some sensitive follow-ups where hallucination risk is a concern.

We're aiming to start an eval on Monday if we can get the runbook + benchmarks today.

— Alice
Director, Product — Conversational AI
Acme Corp

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps (model fit)

Hi Alice — quick answers and links below. Full numbers and logs are in the Drive folder.

- Latency (redwood-13b-q8) at ~15 tps (our test harness emulates steady client concurrency):  
   * median: 210ms
   * p95: 410ms
   * p99: 740ms
   * sustained TPS on a 4xA100 pool: ~60 TPS (single-model pool, batched) — your 15 tps is well within headroom.

- Reducing to redwood-7b-q4: expected latency improves (~120ms median, p95 ~260ms), but quality degrades on complex multi-turn completions. We recommend A/Bing with your prompt set and monitoring NLL / hallucination checks (see prompt_set.csv attached).

- Quality regression risk: medium when moving 13b -> 7b for long-context, instruction-heavy flows. To mitigate:
   1) Run targeted prompt set (attached) and sample-based evals (ROUGE/semantic similarity + manual review).
   2) Use safety-tuned redwood-rlhf-small-v1 as a fallback for sensitive intents.

Links & artifacts: 
- Benchmark folder (full CSVs, raw latency histograms): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDEFghIJkLMnopQrsTuv/acme-benchmarks
- Summary PDF (attached): acme_benchmark_summary.pdf
- Prompt set used for evals: acme_prompt_set.csv
- Redwood-verified profiles: https://redwood-inference.com/verified-profiles/rw-13b-q8

Marissa — can you outline the 24-hour eval config (instance types, batching config, KV caching suggestions) and share a one-page runbook I can pass to Acme?

Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Hi all — adding the 24-hour eval runbook and quick config notes below. Happy to kick off the sandbox on Monday morning if Acme confirms.

24-hour eval — suggested config:
- Deployment: Dedicated single-node (4xA100) or Hosted burst-capable pool (if you prefer managed)
- Model config: start with redwood-13b-q8, then switch to redwood-7b-q4 for A/B in hours 12-18
- Batching: dynamic batching with 64ms max wait (keeps median low while improving throughput)
- KV/prefix caching: enable for repeated conversation prefixes; use 128MB cache per shard
- Metrics to capture: TPS, median/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, failure rate (non-200), hallucination rate (defined via manual sampling and semantic similarity score)

Runbook links: Drive folder above includes the exact infra template and benchmark scripts. I'll run the initial 2-hour smoke test Friday afternoon and share the raw CSVs.

Next steps for Acme: confirm Monday start + Slack channel for results. If you want, we can also add a 1-hr joint review after 24 hours to review tails and quality.

— Marissa
